candidate_findings.subject: Teotihuacan monumental construction fill comparison
candidate_findings.assertion: Torras Freixa distinguishes earth-and-stone fills of Moon Pyramid Buildings 1–3, earth-dominant Building 4, earth/tepetate Sun Pyramid fill, and stone/mud compartment-cell construction of the Feathered Serpent Pyramid, associated with contrasting talud and talud-tablero façades.
candidate_findings.limitations: Building 4 cell-system proposal tentative; comparison not a secure relative dating tool

candidate_findings.subject: Teotihuacan labor-duration model assumptions
candidate_findings.assertion: Torras Freixa reports Murakami's assumptions: one worker per five-person household, five hours per day procurement and transport, eight hours manufacture and assembly, 30/60/100 construction days per year, yielding conditional estimates of under ten years per pyramid; notes 50-year discrepancy in Early Tlamimilolpa placement relative to Rattray chronology.
candidate_findings.limitations: Under ten years is a modeled output, not observed duration; primary Murakami data not checked

enrichment_not_new_findings.assertion: Building 1 base 23.5m, Building 3 base 31.3m, early Moon Pyramid building orientations shift from approx 11° toward 15°30′ east of astronomical north; absence of lime plaster.

Torras Freixa 2018 pp.219–220,225–226,232,235 presents a 200–250 CE monumentalization hypothesis, explicitly dependent on Sugiyama and contested by older construction models and redeposited ceramic fill.
